notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1985:VI.6.27.2 prints UNSTRING identifier-1, [DELIMITED BY [ALL] identifier-2 or literal-1, with repeatable OR [ALL] identifier-3 or literal-2], INTO one or more identifier-4 each with [DELIMITER IN identifier-5] and [COUNT IN identifier-6], then [WITH POINTER identifier-7], [TALLYING IN identifier-8], [ON OVERFLOW imperative-statement-1], [NOT ON OVERFLOW imperative-statement-2] and [END-UNSTRING] in that order. unstringStatement and its phrase rules keep that order (TALLYING before POINTER, COUNT before DELIMITER, a second DELIMITED phrase, a literal sender and DELIMITED BY SIZE are syntax errors) and BindUnstring binds every phrase; the one later relaxation of the operands, a reference-modified identifier-1 (§2002:F.2, item 139), is refused at 85 by VisitUnstringStatement (COBOL0900). Probed at --std 85 with the optional words BY, IN, WITH and ON omitted and with ALL on both delimiter positions. What is NOT implemented is the printed sequence of the two phrases: the conditionalPhrases loop and Associates / MayAssociate ask only that a phrase is one the statement's formats print and is not yet written, with no edition arm, so the NOT phrase written before its positive twin compiles and runs at 85; either order is the 2002 change §2002:F.2 (item 33), which the row's change record names. Same mechanism as the STRING and arithmetic rows of this slice. The witness runs DELIMITED BY ALL, DELIMITER IN, COUNT IN, TALLYING and both phrases in the printed order.
